# Native C++ Big Bang film — development roadmap

**Primary deliverable:** a 300-second, eight-scene, cinematic early-universe animation whose **frames are generated by this native C++ application**. This is the authoritative final implementation repository. Blender/Python in [IKitheka/primordial-universe-animation](https://github.com/IKitheka/primordial-universe-animation) is a visual-design reference and bounded-preview tool, not the production renderer.

**Owner requirement set:** 2026-11-14. **Status:** architecture and quality gates agreed; C++ parity not yet proven. Do not claim that the existing OpenGL prototype already matches the Blender/Cycles version.

## Current codebase baseline

- C++17 / CMake, OpenGL 3.3 core, GLFW, GLAD and GLM. `src/main.cpp` builds a timed `Particle` scene with a core/shockwave and renders `GL_POINTS`.
- `HDRFramebuffer`, `BloomEffect` and GLSL post-processing are present. Reuse after verifying behavior; the existing orange fireball/shockwave is a superseded visual prototype, not an approved aesthetic.
- Time currently depends on `glfwGetTime()`; rendering and exports must instead be frame-addressable and deterministic.
- **No native 300-second, eight-scene cinematic renderer is verified yet.**

## Contract with Blender reference

Scene windows: 00–20 Planck/ignition, 20–50 inflation, 50–90 QGP, 90–130 nucleosynthesis, 130–170 opaque plasma, 170–200 recombination/CMB, 200–240 dark ages, 240–300 first stars/galaxies.

Time sampling: frame `f` (1-indexed) evaluates at `t=(f-1)/FPS`; 9,000 frames @30fps, 18,000 frames @60fps. Frame 1 is 0 s. Never infer a source-frame number using elapsed wall time. Target aspect 16:9; final target 3840×2160, 60fps, with user-approved fallback only. Use explicit seed values, deterministic evaluation order, and timestamp/parameter versioning.

**C++ must render** the film using C++/GLSL calculations (including renderer-controlled rendering/recording), not play or repackage Blender output. Blender camera curves, particle positions, meshes, seeds and selected volumetric data may be imported as inputs; that is not a cheat when the C++ program still performs real shading, scene evaluation, rendering and image export. Python scripts may be used to *author the reference data* or offline assets, but the final C++ render must run independently of Blender/Python.

Scientific visual metaphors are labelled; inflation is not an explosion into pre-existing space, Planck-era imagery is speculative, CMB imagery is illustrative unless a measured map is explicitly sourced. Do not claim pixel-perfect Blender parity or true physics that the engine does not simulate.

## Native nine-stage rendering pipeline

| Stage | Native implementation target |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Scene definition | C++ `SceneState`/per-epoch objects, particles, volumes, cameras, lights, event scheduler |
| 2. Model/world transform | GLM matrix transforms; art-scale convention and stable world coordinates |
| 3. Camera/view transform | time-sampled position/orientation/FOV/focus; explicit view matrix |
| 4. Lighting/shading | GLSL emissive/radiative media and phase approximations; exposure-normalized luminance |
| 5. Projection | GLM perspective/viewport aspect, matched to reference camera intrinsics |
| 6. Clipping/culling | near/far planes, bounding-volume or LOD checks, depth-aware passes |
| 7. Screen mapping | OpenGL viewport, HDR render targets, anti-aliasing, 16:9 pixel export |
| 8. Visibility/ray traversal | explicit depth-tested rasterization and **GLSL volume ray marching**; document this as *not* Cycles BVH path tracing |
| 9. Post-processing | existing HDR FBO, controlled bloom, tone mapping and pixel/sequence export |

**OpenGL compatibility:** existing baseline requests GL 3.3 core; volume ray marching should initially be implemented in fragment shaders and FBO passes. Consider GL 4.3+ compute shaders only as a measured optional path with capability detection/fallback. Avoid unportable NVIDIA-only solutions.

## Milestones and measurable definition of done

### M0 — Native deterministic prototype (immediately)

1. Confirm CMake build on Ubuntu and record renderer/OpenGL version; capture a screenshot/frame from the current native executable.
2. Introduce an animation `Timeline`, `evaluate(seconds)`, `SceneState` and camera settings; do not mix temporal simulation with draw-loop wall clock.
3. Implement `--time`, `--frame`, `--fps`, `--scene`, `--width`, `--height`, `--output` interfaces, with a bounded one-frame PNG export. Keep interactive mode working.
4. Add build and timeline unit tests. If headless rendering is unsupported, test through Xvfb/software Mesa or an explicitly documented workstation path; never silently substitute Blender frames.
5. Define `interop/v1` manifest and two reference-camera samples from the Blender repo.
   
**Gate:** identical frame inputs produce repeatable C++ frames and reference metadata; C++ actually draws pixels.

### M1 — Opening/inflation parity (0–50s)

1. Import or reproduce Blender reference time keys (camera, lens, field density/emission/noise scale/seed and color transform), recording conversion choices.
2. Implement a **continuous 3D fluctuation field** with a volumetric GLSL ray-marching pass; show scale changes as a cinematic metaphor without a white disk, orange explosion, edge-cut sphere, storm cloud haze or radial streaks.
3. Use the current C++ HDR framebuffer with restrained glow/exposure and no hidden scene pop at 20 seconds.
4. Render matched native frames **10, 18, 20, 25, 30, 45, 50 s** and a short consecutive-frame sequence across the 20s boundary.
5. Compare against current-approved Blender reference with exact source SHAs and consistent camera/FOV/tone mapping. Document remaining visual differences, CPU/GPU times and memory.
   
**Gate:** owner reviews and accepts *C++ renders* of the first two scenes; not merely successful CMake/Blender checks.

### M2 — Dense early universe (50–170s)

Native QGP continuum, nucleon fusion closeups and optically thick medium; match reference motion and density; test 50/90/130/170s boundaries.

### M3 — Transparency and structure (170–300s)

Native CMB/decoupling, dark ages, first stars/galaxies; matched visual references and continuous shot transitions. Use plausible procedural astrophysical geometry without claiming a numerical cosmology simulation.

### M4 — Native engineering and production readiness

Implement chunked offline deterministic frame export, checkpoint/resume with source and checksum consistency, output validation, color management/encoding and timeline continuity. Validate 4K stress frames and 30/60 fps consecutive motion tests on available hardware. Estimate time/storage from measured native C++ frames. **Do not render the full 4K movie before source-specific owner approval and cost check.**

### M5 — Final C++ film

Generate the approved full 300-second image sequence with the C++ executable and encode using FFmpeg (external encode tool is acceptable). Deliver executable/source, shaders, manifests, build instructions, performance/validation report and full output. Blender source is included only as optional *reference*, never presented as the final renderer.

## Renderer-neutral scene interchange: v1 design

A documented JSON manifest plus optional binary geometry/volume assets, rather than C++ parsing `.blend` material graphs. Include:
- `schema_version`, `reference_repository`, `reference_commit`, `scene_id`, `seed`, `fps`, `frame_range`, `duration_seconds`, `scale_units`;
- camera keys `time_s`, `position`, `orientation` or target, `focal_length_mm`, `sensor_width_mm`, `near_clip`, `far_clip`, focus distance and interpolation;
- field keys for density, anisotropy, emission intensity, noise/wave scale, spatial transforms and temporal fade; appearance/temperature metadata and explicit color convention;
- optional glTF geometry, typed particle buffers, or documented OpenVDB/3D texture caches, with coordinate handedness and units.

Start with two or three native timestamps to prove interchange before adding complex tooling. Version the schema and attach sample source/preview manifests to PRs. Do not overfit to Blender shader node names: define meaningful physical/art parameters.

## Test matrix / CI

- **C++ checks:** clean configure/build, static/unit tests, deterministic time mapping, simple native PNG/decode, safety bounds. Run native preview with a compatible GL context; record GL version and shader compile warnings.
- **Visual checks:** matched Blender reference vs C++ native stills (10, 18, 20, 25, 30, 45, 50 seconds first), motion continuity and no excessive clipping/whiteout/black screens. Explicit owner review.
- **Regression and provenance:** C++ commit SHA, Blender reference SHA, schema version, seeds, scene params, preview settings and frame hashes.
- **Budget/permissions:** preview first. No unapproved 4K full sequence, cloud GPUs, expensive runners or new credentials. Main branch changes only through reviewed PRs. Avoid touching other active Codex work.

## Immediate next coding ticket

**M0 first deliverable:** a C++ PR that adds a deterministic `--time` / `--frame` evaluation path and native one-frame PNG capture while preserving interactive mode; CI proves the code builds. Then begin the M1 volume shader port in parallel with visual work in the Blender repo.

Reference plan: [Blender-side C++ portability plan](https://github.com/IKitheka/primordial-universe-animation/blob/plan/cpp-final-delivery-contract/docs/CPP_PORTABILITY_PLAN.md). When it is merged, switch this link to the default branch.
